highlights.title: PostgreSQL is the source of truth; Redis is a rebuildable dispatch index.
details: tradeoff: two writes per dispatch, plus reconciler complexity.
rejected: *Redis-only state (RQ/Celery style).* State is lost on Redis failover, and querying and listing are weak.
*PostgreSQL-only queue using `SKIP LOCKED` polling.* Simpler, but worker polling puts load on the primary at scale, and the requirements call for Redis. It stays as a possible degraded mode.

highlights.title: Claims are fenced by a CAS `UPDATE` in PostgreSQL with a per-claim `lease_token`.
rejected: *Redis reliable queue (`LMOVE` into a processing list).* Redis isn't durable enough to act as the authority.
*Redlock.* Unsafe under clock jumps and GC pauses.

highlights.title: Short leases with heartbeat renewal, kept separate from the job timeout.
details: tradeoff: heartbeat write load, about `running_jobs / 15` updates per second.
rejected: *an SQS-style visibility timeout equal to the job timeout*, where a crashed hour-long job would sit locked for an hour.

highlights.title: Delayed, scheduled, and retrying jobs live only in PostgreSQL and are promoted by the scheduler.
details: tradeoff: about 1 s of scheduling precision.
rejected: *a Redis delayed ZSET*, which would create a second source of truth for timing.

highlights.title: Leaderless scheduler loops using `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`.
details: tradeoff: every loop must be idempotent, which is enforced in review and tests.
rejected: *leader election with an advisory lock or a Redis lock.* It adds failover gaps and split-brain cases.

highlights.title: One Redis sorted set per queue, with a composite priority and FIFO score.
details: tradeoff: low priorities can starve. Aging is deferred to Later.
rejected: *Redis Streams.* The consumer-group PEL duplicates the PostgreSQL leasing, and Streams have no priority.
*One list per priority level.* More keys, and every level has to be blocked on.

highlights.title: Async-first worker runtime: one event loop per process with M slots, scaled out by processes.
rejected: *Prefork process pools.* Complex supervision and IPC.

highlights.title: At-least-once execution with an idempotent-handler contract.
rejected: *exactly-once through distributed transactions.* It isn't achievable with arbitrary external side effects.

highlights.title: Prefixed API keys stored as HMAC-SHA256 with a versioned pepper.
rejected: *bcrypt or argon2.* Adds around 50 ms to every request.

highlights.title: The DLQ is the `dead` status in PostgreSQL, not a separate queue.
Running jobs are cancelled cooperatively, on a best-effort basis.
rejected: *hard-killing worker tasks.* It corrupts handler state and shared connections.

highlights.title: The worker dashboard is built in Grafana, not as a custom UI.
